acceptance: one text document per record carrying source file + archive sha256 through the existing encoder; a stated bounded sample with the fraction recorded; chemistry queries go to the structured index, not the fabric
defects_found: the molecule table held 2,897,819 rows with smiles NULL and props = 'chembl_id' -- a 'fully ingested' ChEMBL release that stored identifiers only, so P4's own fork (chemistry to the structured index) led nowhere until structures were derived for 6.90% of it.

the assistant's first denominator for ethics_commonsense.csv was line-counted (54,093); the file has quoted multi-line fields and the csv module gives 13,910, matching the platform's own earlier ingest. Fixed, and the ingest now prunes before replacing so no stale documents survive a correction.
the ingestion design doc's chembl_37.sdf.gz size (701 MB) is stale: the file is 931,156,420 B.
ed_train.csv is a 14-byte truncated download, counted and refused as a corpus.
measurement_corrections: the design assumed ~169 docs/s; measured 1,126.8 docs/s, so its arithmetic over-states the cost of any sample by ~6.7x.
the kernel parses the index once per process (OnceLock), so an ingest is invisible to the running kernel until it restarts: 4.9 s from stop to /health with the 53.2 MB index.
stated_limits: 1.09% of the available relational records; 6.90% of the molecule rows; no substructure search (no fingerprint index exists); the fabric's short-query discrimination is unchanged by this and was not re-measured.
runtime_probe_note: the seal's first probe indexed the response as a list; /k3/retrieve returns an object with the ranked list under `results`. The probe was wrong, not the kernel. Corrected here and in the seal script.
